title: Connect Database
summary: DB = automation memory — a single location with fixed fields for writing and reading.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Automation becomes more powerful when it stores organized data — not just sends a message and forgets.
- Why now? The workflow reads and writes — without a clear place for data, repetitive tasks revert to manual work.
- What after the lesson? You will choose where the workflow stores the data and what fields it needs.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- "The client registered — but we can't find their data."
- Automation sends a welcome email — good. But when sales asks, "Who is this client?" — there’s no record.
- The data only went to email — not in an organized place that can be referenced daily.
- The default worker needs memory: Where to save? What fields? When to read? — without that, repetitive tasks revert to manual work.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: DB = Automation Memory
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Every lead or request needs to be recorded in one place — a table or organized sheet with fixed fields.
- Write: When is the data written? (After registration) — When is it read? (Daily report, follow-up).
- Three fields are enough to start: Name, Contact, Date/Status — you don’t need 20 columns.
- The workflow reads from the same place it writes — this is what makes repetitive tasks work automatically.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Email Only vs Organized Record
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Email Only | Record + Email |
|----------|------------|
| Automation sends an email — the data is in the inbox. After a week: Who registered? No one knows. | The same automation writes a row in a table (Name, Phone, Date) + sends an email. Follow-up is automatic.

sections.heading: Screenshot Block
sections.contentMarkdown: Every event (registration, progress, request) is recorded in one place. The workflow reads and writes from the same source — not scattered files.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Automation records new clients every day. Sales needs a report with their names. What is most important?
The workflow writes each client in an organized table with fixed fields — and reads from it for the report.
Explanation: An organized record = the memory of automation. An email without a table = repetitive work returns to manual.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Define Where Data Is Stored
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The mission is design — not a mandatory technical connection. Choose a workflow and define: Where is the data stored? What fields? AI can suggest columns — you choose the final ones. Submission: Workflow · Storage location · At least 3 fields · When to write (after which trigger) · When to read (who uses it and why) Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Location + Fields | 60% | A defined storage location — not "we'll see"; at least 3 fields with clear names |
| Writing and Reading | 40% | When to write linked to the trigger; when to read with a clear user.
